historical_references.reference: Miran ibn Muhammad, a Persian poet and scholar of the Iranian Sassanid period, is known for his works in Persian and Arabic languages. He wrote extensively on various topics including poetry, history, and philosophy. Miran was born in Khorasan and studied under the tutelage of several renowned scholars. He is considered one of the pioneers of the Persian language in the Islamic world and a significant contributor to early Islamic literature.

historical_references.reference: Miran Shah, a Turco-Mongol ruler of the Timurid Empire, ruled in Central Asia from 1405 to 1409 AD. He is remembered for his military campaigns against the Golden Horde and the Mongol Oirats, extending the Timurid Empire's territories significantly. Miran Shah was a son of Miranshah, the eldest son of Timur, and was appointed as the governor of Transoxania after his father's death. He later succeeded his father as the ruler of the Timurid Empire after a power struggle.
